subject: Rivermind capacity sketch & runway: tokens/sec, SLO fit, headroom
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Monroe <alex@rivermind.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Rivermind capacity sketch & runway: tokens/sec, SLO fit, headroom

Alex — thanks for the traffic details on the call earlier. I pulled together a lightweight sketch (attached) to align on the committed capacity needed to hit your p95 SLO and buffer for peak campaigns. High level asks: can you confirm the average generated tokens per request and peak concurrent QPS for the demo / launch phases?

Summary of what I built into the sheet (attached):
- Input traffic: baseline qps, nightly lull, weekend multiplier, marketing-campaign spike (15–20x)
- Per-call token distribution (prompt, generation avg, 90th pct) — configurable
- Model variants: rdx-13B (q8_0), rdx-30B (q4_0), fallback small model (rdx-7B)
- Latency budget: target p95 <= 350ms for online assistant flows; batch-friendly endpoints for async workloads
- Headroom targets: 40% sustained cushion, 2x spike absorb for short bursts (<=5 min)

Initial assumptions I used (open to tuning):
- Avg tokens per call: 72 (prompt 18 + gen 54)
- Peak sustained QPS for launch: 40, marketing spike peak QPS: 600 (15x)
- Tokens/sec at baseline peak = 40 * 72 = 2,880 t/s; spike = 600 * 72 = 43,200 t/s

What I need from you to finalize tonight:
1) Confirm avg tokens per call and expected demo vs launch QPS (Alex)
2) Prioritize SLO: is p95 350ms firm or flexible to 500ms in exchange for lower cost?
3) Any data locality / region constraints that require dedicated nodes in multiple regions?

Next steps: Priyom / Karthik — once Alex confirms the inputs, can you produce two sizing options in the sheet: "Cost-Optimized" (quantized heavy + KV caching aggressive, 30% headroom) and "SRE-Heavy" (40–50% headroom, faster model variant primary)?

Thanks — Hannah

--

Subject: Re: Rivermind capacity sketch & runway: tokens/sec, SLO fit, headroom

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side:
- Average tokens per API request: 80 (prompt ~20, gen ~60). Marketing CTA flows push gen to ~140 tokens on the high end (longer responses).
- Launch baseline QPS: 50 (we expect the demo to not exceed this); marketing spike estimate: 750 QPS sustained for ~3–10 minutes (short bursts) — historic click-through behavior from our pre-launch tests.
- SLO: p95 350ms is our customer promise; we can tolerate brief degradations during marketing bursts but want transparent fallback (smaller model or queueing) rather than hard failures.
- Region: US-first; APAC expansion later this year. No immediate EU requirement.

Attaching sample request traces (we will share the CSV) and the high-level product schedule. Happy to hop on a 30-min sizing call if that helps.

— Alex

Subject: Re: Rivermind capacity sketch & runway: tokens/sec, SLO fit, headroom

Thanks — used Alex's updated numbers to run a first-pass capacity map. Key notes from the quick sim (sheet attached as CSV):
- Baseline (50 QPS * 80 t/c) = 4,000 t/s sustained. Marketing spike (750 QPS * 80 t/c) = 60,000 t/s.
- Model throughput (measured on our internal rdx-13B q8_0 profile): ~2,700 t/s per GPU for steady-state short responses (this assumes batched decoding with 8 concurrent requests and KV cache hit > 60%). For long-form generation (140 tokens avg) effective sustained t/s drops ~30% due to decode length and memory pressure.
- Sizing options:
  - Cost-Optimized: primary rdx-13B (q8_0), aggressive KV caching, 40 GPUs dedicated in US region. Provides ~35–40% headroom under baseline, can absorb marketing spike for short bursts by autoscaling to a reserved burst pool + fallback to rdx-7B for tails. Estimated monthly committed cost (GPU hours): X (see sheet).
  - Resilience-First: mix rdx-30B (q4_0) for low-latency priority routes (10 GPUs) + rdx-13B fleet (60 GPUs) as main slab. Target p95 < 350ms across priority endpoints with 50% headroom, marketing spike handled by temporary burst slab + model degradation policy. Estimated committed cost: ~2.1x Cost-Optimized.
- Notes on tail latency: KV cache warm-up needed; cold-start requests (new prefixes) can add 100–180ms. We recommend a short pre-warming strategy for promotional blasts (pre-cache expected prefixes).

Open questions for sizing decision:
- Which endpoints are priority (must keep p95 350ms) vs background (can accept queued or async responses)?
- Acceptable monthly committed spend range from the customer side (Alex) — this will determine model mix.

I'll refine the sheet after Alex confirms priority endpoints.

--

Subject: Re: Rivermind capacity sketch & runway: tokens/sec, SLO fit, headroom

Brief technical addendum from infra:
- The per-GPU t/s number Priyom used (2,700 t/s) is realistic for rdx-13B q8_0 under optimistic batching and >60% KV cache hits. For our safety calculations, use a conservative operational throughput of 2,100 t/s per GPU to account for longer tails, telemetry overhead, and multi-tenant jitter.
- Using 2,100 t/s conservative baseline:
  - Baseline (4,000 t/s) -> requires 2 GPUs (4,000/2,100 = 1.9 -> round up). Add 40% headroom -> 3 GPUs dedicated min.
  - Spike (60,000 t/s) -> requires 29 GPUs at conservative throughput. To absorb spike with 2x short burst buffer we recommend: reserved slab 40 GPUs + burst pool (cloud autoscale) and fallback policy.
- Recommendation: commit a base slab of 20 GPUs (to cover baseline + buffer across multiple priority endpoints) + a reserved burst pool of 20 GPUs (lower priority, warm) that can be promoted. This balances committed cost and operational runway.
- Quantization tradeoffs: q4_0 on rdx-30B cuts cost per effective t/s but increases p95 by ~10–25ms in our measurements. Reserve rdx-30B for high-priority flows where semantics matter.

I will draft a short runbook for promotional pre-warm (steps to push expected prompts to KV cache 30–60 minutes before blast) and include it in the sheet.

— Karthik

Thanks everyone — this is helpful and aligns with what I expected. Quick action items before Friday:
- Alex: confirm which endpoints are "priority" (customer-facing assistant flows) vs "background" (analytics, batch rerank). Also confirm an acceptable committed monthly spend range so we can pick Cost-Optimized vs Resilience-First.
- Priyom & Karthik: combine your two sizing options into a single one-page decision table in the sheet (I want: capacity (GPUs), expected p95, estimated committed cost, fallback policy summary, pre-warm runbook link).
- Laura: please prepare a short note on contract language for burst pools and reserved capacity (SLA implications) and add HubSpot deal notes.

If Alex is available, let's do a 30-min call tomorrow to finalize inputs and I can send a commercial sketch by EOD Friday. If not, we'll proceed off email.

Thanks — Hannah
